entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 2006 H.B. 1380) and verified exact source and subsection fingerprints. Confirmed permissive commission authority to seek government or private project assistance in sub 1, and revised sub 2 title to include the mandatory security proviso qualifying permissive comprehensive-agreement project loans to the private partner; retained sub 1.

headings.title: Agreed project financing terms, revenues, and obligations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2006 H.B. 1380). Covers project financing amounts and terms set in interim or comprehensive agreements, use of available revenues, and lawful issuance of debt, equity, or other obligations.

headings.title: Private partner bonds, security limits, nonrecourse status, and tax exemption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers private partner bond and obligation issuance, commission assistance contracts, bar on encumbering state or public eminent-domain property, exclusive private partner liability and face-of-bond disclaimer, and Missouri tax exemption except estate tax.

headings.title: Contracts for state road bond issuance and proceeds loans
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers permissive contracting for the commission to issue state road bonds for the project and loan the proceeds to the private partner.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and history note (L. 2006 H.B. 1380) and verified exact source and subsection fingerprints. Verified agreed financing terms and revenue/debt/equity authority in sub 1, private partner bond issuance, eminent-domain encumbrance bar, nonrecourse status/face disclaimer, and Missouri tax exemption except state estate tax in sub 2, and state road bond loan contracts in sub 3. All 3 drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Commission authority to condemn project lands
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2006 H.B. 1380). Covers permissive commission authority to condemn lands for the project in the name of the state of Missouri.

headings.title: Chapter 523 condemnation procedure and private partner payment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs commission action under chapter 523 to condemn fee simple or other land interests when necessary and requires private partner payment of condemnation amounts under the comprehensive agreement.

headings.title: Private partner survey entry after notice and damage liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers permissive private partner entry onto property subject to taking after prior owner notice to survey route and design, and liability for all property damages resulting from the inspection.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and history note (L. 2006 H.B. 1380) and verified exact source and subsection fingerprints. Checked permissive commission condemnation authority in sub 1, chapter 523 procedure and private partner payment obligation in sub 2, and private partner notice-conditioned survey entry and inspection damage liability in sub 3 (revised sub 3 reviewNote to remove the unstated term "strict liability"). All 3 drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: User-fee collection methods and windshield electronic devices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 2006 H.B. 1380). Covers permissive private partner toll collection and enforcement methods and legality of authorized windshield electronic devices unless obstructing the operator's clear view; retains original-rolls footnote '*Word "are" appears in original rolls.' for 'is'.

headings.title: Required plain-view toll violation notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Sets out verbatim required notice posted in plain view at toll facilities advising motorists that failure to pay is a traffic violation reported to law enforcement.

headings.title: Infraction penalty and unpaid toll remittance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Makes vehicle owners failing to pay required tolls guilty of an infraction and requires remitting the unpaid toll to the private partner plus a fine up to $200 upon conviction.

headings.title: Evidence admissibility, rebuttable presumption, co-owners, and rental vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes. Covers foundation-qualified admissibility of reports, calls, and photo-monitoring evidence, rebuttable presumption of violation, single-owner conviction and cost limit for multiple owners, and rental/leasing company rebuttal and registered-mail pre-prosecution notice protections.

headings.title: Toll violation reporting, citations, prosecution, and other traffic offenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 including subdivisions (1) through (3), continuation paragraph, and source notes. Covers toll-operator phone and sworn photo-monitoring reports (prima facie evidence with inspection rights), law enforcement citation and prosecution authority, and the continuation paragraph preserving citations for other project traffic violations.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections (including subdivisions (1)–(3), paragraphs (a)–(b), and the continuation paragraph of sub 5) and all source notes (L. 2006 H.B. 1380; original-rolls footnote "*Word 'are' appears in original rolls." at sub 1) and verified exact source and subsection fingerprints. Verified windshield device legality limit in sub 1, verbatim posted toll notice in sub 2, infraction penalty and unpaid-toll remittance in sub 3, foundation/rebuttable-presumption/co-owner/rental-vehicle rules in sub 4, and reporting, citations, prosecution, and the continuation paragraph preserving citations for other project traffic laws in sub 5. All 5 drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Tort liability caps aligned with section 537.610
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2006 H.B. 1380). Establishes per-person and per-occurrence tort liability caps for private partners, employees, agents, and insureds under sections 227.600 to 227.669 identical to section 537.610 caps as annually adjusted under section 537.610(5).

headings.title: Insurance not expanding statutory tort liability caps
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Prohibits using commercial general liability insurance purchased by a private partner under sections 227.600 to 227.669 to expand the tort liability caps imposed in this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 2006 H.B. 1380) and verified exact source and subsection fingerprints. Confirmed private-partner per-person and per-occurrence tort liability caps aligned with § 537.610 and annual Implicit Price Deflator adjustments under § 537.610(5) in sub 1, and prohibition on commercial general liability insurance expanding those caps in sub 2. Both titles retained.

headings.title: Material default notice and opportunity to cure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2006 H.B. 1380). Requires commission notice of material default and opportunity to cure for the private partner and comprehensive-agreement financing providers before exercising section remedies.

headings.title: Permissive commission remedies during continuing material default
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (4) and history note. Preserves permissive ('may') commission remedies during continuing material default: bond claims under section 227.633, certified-mail termination and legal/equitable remedies, chapter 523 condemnation with financing-provider standing, and user-fee collection under section 227.660.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections (including subdivisions (1)–(4) of sub 2) and history note (L. 2006 H.B. 1380) and verified exact source and subsection fingerprints. Verified pre-remedy material default notice and opportunity to cure for private partner and financing providers in sub 1, and permissive commission remedies during continuing material default (citing § 227.633, ch. 523 with financing-provider standing, and § 227.660) in sub 2. Both drafted titles retained as accurate.
